proposal: AUDIT (read from the supplied code; nothing executed). (1) Local-to-global is sound as written. _verify_certificate builds blocks from every clause of the dense original, requires every form a block references to lie inside that block's support, and compares F with Q(Px) on all 2^w local points. Conjunction over blocks gives F(X)=Q(PX) globally, and the entrywise P*L=I check gives surjectivity by linearity. I find no omitted-block defect. (2) Skips are sound: every skip returns the original input, and the core path trusts only the subset gate, a self-verified compression and 2-SAT. (3) Cost gaps, not soundness gaps: the 8M figure covers verifier work only. Discovery separately does |z|^2 stabilizer tests per block, a 2^w annihilator enumeration even for a one-clause block (polynomial only because w<=8), a |candidates|*|blocks| ranking, and a fresh basis() per candidate. Under the caps I estimate 1e7-1e8 primitive operations that no receipt counts. The verifier's final r*r*n+work test runs after the matrix loop, so it reports rather than pre-bounds. (4) step() is memoised on pre-canonical states, so refute() reruns on equal canonical inputs, consistent with the observed 4/12 repeats. MECHANISM: gainful biclique refactoring (GBR), the exact inverse of the deployed DP step. This is bounded variable addition (Manthey-Heule-Biere 2012); the mathematics is not new. What I propose is a certified integration plus a work potential. Rule: if F contains every clause (l OR C) for l in a literal set L and C in a clause set K, where no C mentions a variable of L, pick a fresh x and replace those |L||K| clauses by {l OR x : l in L} and {NOT x OR C : C in K}. Soundness (restricted, elementary, needs one generic Lean lemma): F(a) holds iff some b gives F'(a,x=b), because resolving F' on x returns exactly the removed clauses. Only equisatisfiability is used. The rule rewrites only the biclique, so arbitrary extra clauses neither block it nor need to respect it; any rule that needs F to factor through (a OR a') is destroyed by one extra clause mentioning a alone. Acceptance: gainful means |L||K| > |L|+|K|. A compound move is a non-gainful refactoring followed at once by size-nonincreasing DP on variables of L, accepted only if the potential drops, else rolled back. Potential: Phi = 2*(clauses) + (variables). canon, SCC merging, accepted DP, gainful GBR and accepted compound moves each lower Phi by at least 1. Hence any closure sequence has at most 2m+n moves, never exceeds m clauses or n+m variables, and stays within m(n+m)ceil(log2(2(n+m))) bits. This is a theorem candidate about preprocessing length only. NEON58: in the 16-variable quotient each side is the full product of four pairs of negative literals. Gainful steps are L={-a1,-a1'} against 8 links (16 clauses to 10), then L={-a2,-a2'} against 4 links (8 to 6). The last two pairs are 2x2 and 2x1, not gainful alone, but compound moves succeed because each pair variable then occurs negatively once, so DP replaces k+1 clauses by k. Predicted output over both sides: 8 variables and 18 clauses, namely the fixture; Phi falls from 112 to 44 through 8 refactorings and 16 eliminations. With gainful-only moves I expect 12 variables, 24 clauses and remaining search (hand derivation, order dependent). Residual on the fixture: pinned v5 skips compression (every block has one forbidden point), the core probe removes nothing, and in the root IALH call every assignment containing a zero fails unit propagation, so window [1,2,3,4] has an empty table: UNSAT with no branching. For k>=6 pairs the width-k negative clause exceeds the 5-variable window, so IALH returns UNKNOWN; I expect root DP to finish instead (u1 has k positive and one negative occurrence, and by hand the pattern persists) in O(k) eliminations of O(k^2) resolvents. TOTAL WORK: detection indexes each clause minus one literal, costing at most O(S^2) literal operations per move at current size S, so O((2m+n) S^2 log(n+m)) bit operations for the closure. Certificates cost the size of the removed clauses per step. That is polynomial but far from quadratic. On the k-pair family, with input about N = k*2^k bits, the closure costs N*polylog(N) and the residual poly(k). None of this bounds the breadth of the layered search on Phi-irreducible inputs. CANNOT HANDLE: (a) Phi-irreducible formulas such as sparse random 3-CNF, where GBR is a no-op. (b) Pigeonhole: pairwise at-most-one bicliques give small gains, but the counting contradiction and the measured IALH cost (windows, tuples, HNF) are untouched. Refactoring may even remove the <=5-variable supports IALH needs, so GBR must be a fallback branch that keeps the original. (c) Non-product transversals: replace the disjoint pairs by overlapping terms, for example consecutive edges of a cycle. The CNF is then the minimal vertex covers (Perrin-many), with few literal bicliques. (d) Factors that are subclauses rather than literals, and products with scattered deletions. (e) Fresh definition clauses are odd one-point blocks, so GBR must run after BLQ compression, never before. INDEPENDENT TESTS for the unimplemented extension: T1, the Neon58 quotient yields the fixture up to renaming. T2, add one asymmetric extra (a1 OR NOT b2) to the quotient: the biclique clauses are untouched, so every gainful refactoring still applies and UNSAT must be preserved; whether the b2 pair is fully eliminated is order dependent.
missing_theorem: Two statements, both unproved. (R) Recovery under extras: let F contain P = L1 x ... x Lk (variable-disjoint literal sets, each |Li|>=2) plus arbitrary clauses E. Prove that a specified deterministic choice rule (say maximum gain, then lexicographic) leaves at most sum|Li| + c clauses descended from P, for every E. Obstacle: a biclique may straddle P and E and fragment the product; the closure is not confluent, and maximum-gain biclique selection is NP-hard, so the rule must be greedy and the proof an exchange argument. (B) Breadth: Phi bounds depth and preprocessing length, not the sum over layers of |S_t|. Even the classical bound |S_t| <= 2^(clauses cut by the order prefix) is not established for the pinned solver. step interleaves DP and SCC with restriction, so a layer state is a function of the previous processed state, not of the raw restriction of the root. Needed: path independence (equal raw restrictions give equal layer states), or a counterexample. This is falsifiable by exhaustive search over small CNFs. Without (B) no cut-width bound on residual work follows. With (B) one obtains only 2^cutwidth, which is not a general SAT bound.
self_attack: 1. This is a classical preprocessing technique. It adds no proof-complexity power beyond bounded extension and cannot make hard formulas easy. 2. Neon58 was never a superpolynomial witness: peak 8 on 2*2^k+k^2 clauses is polynomial in input size. GBR changes the yardstick to poly(k), which is met here only because the factored form is refutable by unit propagation. 3. The k>=6 DP completion and the gainful-only 12/24 figures are hand derivations; earlier hand predictions in this project failed. 4. The compound move is a lookahead with an ad hoc acceptance rule, and (R) may be false for it. 5. Fresh variables need a branching position. A bad placement can raise the peak; the trusted reorder result (8 to 2) shows order matters more than this proposal controls. 6. I cannot see Fable73's text. If its contraction is already a one-directional extension, the delta shrinks to the potential, the compound move and the extras argument. 7. Phi counts moves, not bits per move: DP can widen clauses to n+m literals, so S^2 detection is expensive. 8. The fixture is a control for the post-refactoring target. It is not evidence that GBR is implemented or that discovery finds the bicliques.
mechanism_signature: GBR: biclique extension (inverse DP) with a certified projection step, accepted only when Phi = 2|clauses| + |variables| drops; then the unchanged v5 residual solver (UP-filtered IALH, size-nonincreasing DP).
delta_from_prior: Versus link-twin contraction as summarised in the brief: extension instead of quotient, so the formula need not factor through (a OR a'); literal sets of any size with merely overlapping links; tolerant of arbitrary extras by construction; one potential covering canon, SCC, DP and refactoring; the observation that the 5-variable window cap stops IALH at k>=6; and an explicit statement that path independence of layer states is unproved. Versus GF(2) quotienting: nonlinear and kernel-free, with no stabilizer needed. No new symmetry detector is proposed.
